# `get_obj`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the objects of one named object list.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb57f0, ObjListConfig::Get @0x6c4a90 (64-bit build) |

Returns an array of {name, coord, type} for the list whose display name is given. Unknown or empty groups give 236.

Side effects: Enumerates the XML configuration into local structures and selects the requested group. The established write is creation of a configured lock file under the temporary directory; no list content is changed. Synchronous; no explicit timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_obj"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array | no | - | The list display name, as a bare string or as a one-element array whose first element is used (extra elements ignored). Absent, null, empty array or a non-string gives 105. No length check. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | array<object> | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Objects of the named list; an existing empty list gives an empty array. [READ] |
| `result[].name` | string | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Object display name. [READ] |
| `result[].coord` | array<number> | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Two numbers: RA (hours, INFERRED from add_obj storage) and Dec (degrees, INFERRED). Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `result[].type` | integer | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Opaque client-defined integer, returned exactly as add_obj stored it; the device never acts on it. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (get_obj success reply) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params is absent, null, an empty array, or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 236 | The named group is empty or unmatched, or the inner enumeration found no children | `xml item is not found` |
| 229 | Outer enumeration could not open the XML key (an empty configuration file name also ends here) | `fail to open xml key` |
| 231 | Inner enumeration was given an invalid handle (not independently established as reachable after a successful open) | `xml is not opened` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Lower failures not converted by the enumeration helpers are unresolved. 32-bit lower-branch equivalence is not asserted.

## Example

Request, get:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"get_obj","params":"Winter targets"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_obj","result":[{"name":"Example nebula","coord":[5,20],"type":0}],"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, no-such-list:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_obj","error":"xml item is not found","code":236,"id":82}
```
